## Detailed Findings

#### 1. MCP header env expansion security (mcp, ~3h, SKIP)

- **What**: Kilo #12554 fix MCP header env expansion security holes in five-part series. Multiple vulnerabilities in Kilo's MCP config loading: (1) project kilo.jsonc with {env:...} in MCP headers caused whole config load to fail since 7.4.5, silently removing every MCP (fixes #12319); (2) decoy in-repo {file:} plus any {env:} could read arbitrary paths into remote MCP headers (no fileScope during post-parse header expand); (3) untrusted project MCP headers could read process.env or authEnv secrets; (4) when project config overrode same-named global remote MCP with new URL without restating headers, expanded secret headers from global entry inherited into project scope; (5) mergeConfig mutated caller's patch object. Fixes: leave {env:} literal during untrusted text substitution, expand only remote MCP headers after parse, drop individual MCPs with blocked env refs instead of full set; ban {file:} during MCP header env expansion (post-parse header expand used trusted substitute without fileScope); ban env secret expansion in project MCP headers (reject {env:} and {file:} per entry with warning so sibling MCPs load); drop global MCP headers on project URL retarget (do not inherit when project overrides URL without restating headers); shallow-copy patch before delete p.mcp so probe-then-write updateProjectConfig paths keep mcp on original object; secure layered MCP transitions; expand MCP header env refs without wiping MCP set. Also fix MCP union narrowing in tests, stop saying "header env expansion failed" when only validating.
- **Why**: Alexi has MCP support (src/mcp/client.ts, src/mcp/config.ts) but different architecture. src/mcp/config.ts loadMcpConfig reads mcp-servers.json (dedicated MCP config file, NOT general kilo.json with arbitrary project config). resolveEnvVars does env expansion (only env vars, no {file:} support). Config is NOT project-scoped (one global mcp-servers.json in ~/.alexi/, no per-project MCP config, no untrusted project config that could leak secrets). No remote MCP headers (MCP servers in Alexi are stdio commands only, no remote URL MCP servers with headers). Alexi's MCP architecture already secure by design: no {file:} expansion (resolveEnvVars only handles env vars), no project-scoped MCP config that could read secrets (single global config in ~/.alexi/), no remote MCP header injection surface (no remote MCPs, only local stdio). Would be SKIP (Alexi architecture already secure, no security holes, different config model). Size ~3h if porting was needed (audit MCP config loading, add security tests), but NOT applicable to Alexi. Category: mcp. Priority: SKIP (no security holes, different architecture).
- **Source**: Kilo PR #12554 "fix(config): expand MCP header env refs without wiping MCP set" (merged 2026-08-11, commit sha unknown, five-part series). Full PR body at https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/12554. Root cause: project kilo.jsonc with {env:} in MCP headers failed config load (since 7.4.5); decoy {file:} could read arbitrary paths into remote MCP headers; untrusted project MCP headers read process.env; global MCP headers leaked into project retargets. Fix: leave {env:} literal during untrusted substitution, expand only remote MCP headers after parse, ban {file:}, reject {env:}/{file:} in project MCP headers, drop global headers on URL retarget.
- **Category**: mcp. **Size**: ~3h. **Priority**: SKIP (no security holes, different architecture, Alexi MCP config is isolated).

#### 2. Compaction summarizer max tokens fix (core, ~2h, SKIP)

- **What**: Cline #13137 respect user max output tokens in compaction summarizer requests. Compaction summarizer hardcoded max_tokens to 1024 and VSCode host never mirrored user's Max Output Tokens setting onto providerConfig, so summary requests were always capped at 1024 tokens. Reasoning models can spend entire budget thinking; reasoning stream is discarded, so no summary text arrives and compaction is skipped on every attempt. Fix: (1) mirror maxTokensPerTurn onto providerConfig.maxOutputTokens in VSCode session factory so consumers that build handlers straight from it (compaction summarizer) honor user's setting, matching CLI; (2) resolve summarizer output budget from explicit config, then model info, then knownModels, before default; raise default to 4096; (3) clamp summarizer default output budget by model metadata instead of adopting it (model maxTokens is reported capability, not product default; without explicit config summarizer now requests 4096 default, lowered by model metadata when model reports less, never raised by it; explicit values still win as-is); (4) log diagnostic warning (reasoning chars, incompleteReason, likely cause) when summarizer returns no summary text instead of silently skipping.
- **Why**: Alexi has no compaction summarizer feature (grep 'compact|summarize' in src/ returns only src/core/context.ts summarizeSessionHistory for session context, not multi-turn compaction). Would be LOW priority if Alexi had compaction (fix UX, honor user settings, prevent reasoning models from stalling summarization). Skip for now (no compaction summarizer feature, Alexi has different session management - src/core/sessionManager.ts).
- **Source**: Cline PR #13137 "fix: respect user max output tokens in compaction summarizer requests" (merged 2026-08-11, commit sha unknown). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13137. Root cause: summarizer hardcoded 1024 tokens, VSCode host never mirrored maxTokensPerTurn, reasoning models spent budget thinking with no summary output. Fix: mirror maxTokensPerTurn onto providerConfig.maxOutputTokens, resolve output budget from config/model/default, raise default to 4096, clamp by metadata, log diagnostic warning.
- **Category**: core. **Size**: ~2h. **Priority**: SKIP (no compaction summarizer feature).
